sources.citation: Decker, Ken; Gobak, Fittokka; Danladi, Yakubu; Dabet, Julius; Riepe, Christina; Aregbesola, Adedamola; Abraham, Benard; Lewinan, Andrew; Araokanmi, Thelma. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-010. SIL International. 123 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 6.3 gives a pooled phonetic (consonant) inventory and 6.5.5 a Jimbin-vs-Turdu [h] variation note; Appendix G (p.64) states: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Its own literature list for Zibinju contains no grammar or phonology (Temple 1922, CAPRO 1995, Haruna 2005, Skinner 1977, Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994).

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2015. Comprehensive Bibliography of Chadic and Hausa Linguistics, Third Edition. Bloomington: IUScholarWorks (hdl.handle.net/2022/20576; CC-BY).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No entry anywhere mentions Zumbun, Jimbin or Zibinju. The complete set of North Bauchi ('Warji') keyword entries is: Aliyu 1980 (traditions of origin), Ibriszimow & Ahmed 2013 (Warji passive), Jungraithmayr 1966/67 (Pa'a, Warji specimens), Migeod 1911-13, Skinner 1974b, Skinner 1977d, Takacs 2001, 2002b, 2007. Confirms, as of Dec 2015, that no published grammar, phonology or thesis on Zumbun exists in the Chadicist literature.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. (Jimbin = 'J', 'Vina Zumbun', Hausa Jimbinanci; informant Maigari Audu.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' (group-level, not Jimbin-specific): 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.'

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists at the publisher (DOI recorded); open or paywalled, not checked
sources.note: The catalogue description gives a Zumbun-Hausa wordlist plus grammatical notes written by Schuh; Schuh's Chadic field transcriptions are as a rule fully tone-marked, and Skinner 1977 reports for the group 'three levels and a falling' heard with monosyllabic minimal pairs, so this notebook is the likeliest place where tone-marked Zumbun forms and any first-hand tonal observations exist. No tone analysis is claimed by the record.
